free_tier.stated: Free-model requests (model ids ending in :free) are capped by a table keyed on credits purchased all time, not on account age: 'Less than 10' credits gives 20 requests a minute and 50 requests a day; 'At least 10' credits gives 20 a minute and 1,000 a day. So the allowance with no credits purchased is 50 requests a day, and the 1,000-a-day ceiling requires purchasing credits; the page grants it starting one credit below the table threshold and prints that figure as an unrendered template placeholder. The page also notes 'Making additional accounts or API keys will not affect your rate limits, as we govern capacity globally'.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: the fallback array is where this silently becomes a paid lane: a pipeline that lists a paid model as fallback bills for every request the free model refuses, which is why the free router (openrouter/free) is the only safe chain.

limits.value: 50 requests a day binds and it is a request count, not a token count: a 1,000-item job takes 20 days on the no-card lane, and the 20 rpm cap means the day's 50 requests are spent in under three minutes of traffic.

notes: The 1,000-requests-a-day figure is not the free tier; it is the post-purchase tier. The no-card ceiling is 50 a day, which is 1,500 a month and is a chat allowance. inference/openrouter-free-ids holds the endpoint and the 401 on an unauthenticated call.
